ecosystem.description: Usurance's internal-role ecosystem: usurance-admin grants and revokes employee role credentials.

governance.transition_plan: No phase transition expected; key rotation is handled by KERI key state, not document transition.

roles.description: The executive accountable for the underwriting result, who decides whether a product exists at all. In this micro-app the CUO does exactly one thing: opens scope, by declaring that a product shall exist for one line of business in one jurisdiction. She does not assemble coverages, author rate tables, or file anything -- that is the designer's, the actuary's and the filing specialist's work. She is also not a work-order dispatcher: she does not know who the actuaries are and does nothing to reach them.

The credentialed professional who builds a rate program and puts their name to it. Their real work happens in Excel and in `ipd-parse` -- unwitnessed, ungated, and deliberately outside this framework -- and this micro-app is only the moment that work becomes a fact someone else can check. They do not decide whether a product exists (the CUO's mandate does) and they do not assemble it (the designer does); they attest that a specific set of bytes is their professional work for a specific mandate.

The role that turns attested pieces into a product. The designer does not decide whether a product should exist (the CUO's mandate does) and does not build the rates (the actuary does); they ASSEMBLE — accepting attested rate programs into a bundle that is, once assembled, the first artifact in this slice that can be called a product at all. Publishing it is somebody else's job and is out of scope.
